# Operator runbook: driving `bin/eccode-gf.js` through one small project (S3 shape)

Evidence tags: [V] verified by running it in a throwaway project here, [C] verified by reading the code, [I] inferred, not run.
Probe projects: `.../scratchpad/rb-probe/p2` (full G1, build, merge, closure, all [V]). Reusable, verified templates (not repo files):
`rb-probe/gen-bundle.js` (valid G1 bundle for the S3 idea, 7 operations, groups api/backend/test), `rb-probe/drive-g1.sh` (init to seal),
`rb-probe/app-files.sh` (sample app that passes ruff and pytest), `rb-probe/handoff.py` (valid handoff JSON). `validate` accepts the bundle on the first try.

## 0. Invocation and environment

- CLI: `node /home/user/ECCode/bin/eccode-gf.js --root <projdir> <command> ...` (also `ECCODE_ROOT`). `--actor <role>` or `ECCODE_ACTOR`. `--json` for JSON. Exit 0 ok, 1 usage, 2 refused by a rule. [V]
- Frozen CLI is still needed for: `design alternatives|decide|adr`, `request ambiguity|assume|clarify`, `evidence run`, `plan checkpoint`, `task reset|waive-budget|list|next|rescope`, `fix verify`, `gate show`: `node /home/user/ECCode/bin/eccode.js --root <projdir> ...`. [V for design, evidence run, plan checkpoint, task reset]
- Project dir must be a git repo with at least one commit, on a branch (not detached): claim baseCommit, `commit`, `merge`, `close` need it. `init` alone works without git. [V/C]
- Python for the sandbox: system `python3` is 3.13 WITHOUT fastapi. Use the prebuilt venv. Before every engine call: `export PATH=/root/.cache/eccode/phase3-venv/bin:$PATH ECCODE_GF_PYTHON=/root/.cache/eccode/phase3-venv/bin/python`. PATH (absolute entries outside the project) is passed into the sandbox; with system python `deps install` fails `Permission denied: /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages` [V]. Venv has fastapi 0.162.1, sqlalchemy 2.1.8, alembic 1.20.1, httpx, pydantic 2.14.3, pytest 9.0.1, uvicorn. `ruff` 0.16.9 is `/root/.local/bin/ruff`. semgrep, gitleaks, trivy, bwrap are NOT installed [V].
- `isolation check` here: `ok:true usable:["landlock"]` (ABI 7, bwrap absent, pid namespace yes, UDP egress open L-GF-79). Group mode is available. [V]
- Refusals leave NO event in the log (only `review.rejected` for gate reviews): friction metrics (S3 B3.4) must be logged by the operator. [V: event count unchanged after refused run/claim]
- Enforcement regimes: bare CLI = text-level (preflight warns L-GF-17, harmless). `node bin/eccode.js install --target <dir> --profile guard|no-shell|sandbox` installs runtime to `.claude/eccode`, 15 agents, hook, `.mcp.json` with one role-locked server per role; profile `no-shell` also denies Bash to everybody incl. the main session [V for `no-shell` output, preflight then says managed-path]. Without install, the main session (orchestrator) may run `--actor <any role>` and write any non-record path. I drove the probe that way.

## A. `init`

`eccode-gf init --root <dir> --name <n> --idea "<text>" [--stack python-fastapi-sqlalchemy-sqlite]` (only stack accepted; another is GF-INIT-1; a second init or an existing ECCode project is GF-INIT-1; actor defaults to orchestrator). [V]
Creates `.eccode/{state.json,events.jsonl,config.json,.gitignore}` and empty dirs `artifacts evidence reviews handoffs memory delivery`. Writes into config.json: `gf:{enabled:true,schemaVersion:1,stackProfile}`, `limits.maxConcurrency=4`, `roles.phase.authors` += integration-engineer, database-engineer, security-engineer, `roles.design.reviewers` += security-reviewer. Does NOT set `gf.isolation` (absent = `kernel`; `"copy"` is the owner's fallback) and leaves `lean.level:"full"`. Track = greenfield, gate order architecture, design, plan, phase:*, verification. [V/C]
Later directories: `.eccode/design/<dd>.md` (ADRs), `.eccode/contracts/<sha>.json` (seal snapshots), `.eccode/handoffs|reviews|evidence/`, `.gf-worktrees/<group>/` (D).

Actors (config + `lib/greenfield/constants.js`):
| Role | May |
|---|---|
| orchestrator | start gates, name reviewers, `gate start phase:*`, `merge`, `deps install`, `close dispatch/battery/slice`, `plan checkpoint`, `task reset|waive-budget`, `evidence run`, `seal`, `estimate revise`, `config pin`; not in any group |
| user | `close accept`, `close resolve --resolution deferred`, `task rescope` (reviewed plan), reopening escalated gates; hook asks the human |
| product-architect / architecture-reviewer | author / review `architecture` gate |
| technical-designer | author `design` gate. technical-reviewer + security-reviewer review it (BOTH required) |
| delivery-lead | author `plan` gate and the phase/verification submissions; technical-reviewer reviews plan and phase gates |
| groups (role -> group): integration-engineer->api, backend-engineer->backend, database-engineer->db, security-engineer->security, frontend-engineer->frontend, test-engineer->test, delivery-lead + devops-engineer->delivery | claim/complete tasks, `run`, `commit`, messages. ai-engineer and learning-debugger are phase authors in no group (cannot complete GF tasks: GF-OWN-3) |
| closing reviewers | any role in `config.roles.*.reviewers` (technical-reviewer, security-reviewer, architecture-reviewer) that has no claim/completion/gate submission in the record |

## B. G1 gates (artifact names are FIXED; matched by basename; each name belongs to exactly one gate)

Locations by convention (tests use these): `.eccode/artifacts/{brief.md,prd.json,architecture.json,spec.md,threat-model.json,plan.json,breakdown.json,estimates.json}` and `contracts/{openapi,db-schema,migrations-plan,access-matrix,fixtures}.json` (+ optional `contracts/events.json`). Contract files MUST be at `contracts/<name>` (GF-ART-2). The PRD is `prd.json` (any dir; `.eccode/artifacts/prd.json` by convention) and is part of the seal. Regular files only (no symlinks), valid JSON, BOM tolerated, <= 8 MiB, one file per basename per submission. `eccode-gf validate <gate> --artifact <f> ...` is a dry run (exit 2 with `- RULE: message`); always run it before `gate submit`. [V]

Frozen-gate requirements (not GF rules) [C]: the `architecture` submission must include a `.md` whose headings contain Users, Problem, Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, Architecture, Assumptions, Open Questions, Risks; the `design` submission a `.md` with Components, Interface Contracts, Data Design, Security, Testing Strategy, Deployment (else MISSING_SECTIONS); not all artifacts may be empty (EMPTY_ARTIFACT); plan gate imports tasks from the FIRST `.json` artifact so list `plan.json` first (GF-WBS-1 else).

Common gate commands [V]:
- `gate start <gate> --actor orchestrator [--reviewers a,b]`. Predecessor gate must be approved (GATE_BLOCKED). `design`: must pass `--reviewers technical-reviewer,security-reviewer` (GF-THR-1 otherwise) and only the orchestrator names reviewers. `plan` start refused while a blocking ambiguity is open (AMBIGUITY_OPEN).
- `gate submit <gate> --actor <author> --artifact <f> ... [--responds-to <last review id>] [--notes t]`. Author roles: architecture=product-architect, design=technical-designer, plan=delivery-lead. Stage rules run first; a refusal commits nothing. After `changes_requested` a resubmission must pass `--responds-to <review id>` (RESPONSE_REQUIRED). Editing a file after submit makes the submission stale: resubmit.
- `gate review <gate> --actor <reviewer> --file <review.json>` (the file path is relative to cwd).

Review JSON (schemas/review.schema.json, additionalProperties false) [V]:
```
{ "decision": "approve" | "changes_requested",
  "summary": "<>=20 chars>",
  "criteria": [ { "id": "C1", "description": "<>=5>", "met": true, "evidence": ["artifact:<path>[#anchor]" | "ev:<evidenceId>"], "notes"?: "" } ],   // >=1 criterion
  "findings": [ { "id": "F1" (^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$), "severity": "blocking|major|minor|info", "title": "<>=5>", "detail": "<>=10>", "recommendation": "<>=5>", "evidence"?: [...], "status"?: "open|resolved" } ],
  "resolvedFindings"?: [ { "id", "resolution": "<>=10>", "evidence": [>=1] } ] }
```
Approve needs: every criterion met with >=1 evidence; every `artifact:` ref in the submission or an earlier approved gate's artifacts; every `ev:` ref exists and passed; no open blocking/major finding; earlier open findings resolved via `resolvedFindings`; reviewer in the gate's reviewers and not an author of it; submitted files unchanged since submit. `changes_requested` needs >=1 blocking/major finding with a recommendation. 3 rejections escalate to the user (`gate reopen --actor user`). Approve of a GF gate also needs GF-ART-1 (the latest submission was registered by the GF submit). Design is approved only when BOTH technical-reviewer and security-reviewer approve the same submission. [C]

### Gate 1 `architecture` (product-architect; architecture-reviewer): files `brief.md`, `prd.json`, `architecture.json`
Prerequisite records (frozen CLI, as product-architect or orchestrator): per technology choice `design alternatives --file opt.json` (JSON list >=2 `{id,title,tradeoffs:{complexity,risk,performance,security,reversibility}}` each text >=10 chars) -> `design decide --file dec.json` (`{alternatives:<da id>,chosen,rationale>=20,rejected:[{option,why}] for EVERY other option,interfaces:[]}`) -> `design adr --decision <dd id>`. One decision per choice (never reused). [V]
- GF-PRD-1 (schema `schemas/gf-prd.schema.json`, no extra keys): `problem` >=80 chars; `users[>=1]{id,description>=5,goals[>=1 of >=3 chars]}`; `scope[>=1]{id ^S-[A-Z0-9-]+$,statement>=5}`; `nonGoals[>=1]`; `ambiguityScan`; `criteria[>=1]{id ^AC-[0-9]+$,statement>=10,covers[>=1],priority P0|P1|P2,verify}`. Also: duplicate scope/criterion/user ids; a criterion covering an unknown scope id; a scope item no criterion covers.
- GF-PRD-2: every criterion needs `verify` with kind http (`operationId`,`as`,`expect.status` int; optional free-form `request`), flow (`steps[>=1]{operationId,as,expect.status}`), command (`run`,`expectExit` int) or browser (`script`,`expect` object); `manual` etc refused.
- GF-PRD-3: `ambiguityScan` is `{"none":true,"justification":">=20 chars"}` ONLY when no question was recorded with `request ambiguity`; otherwise an array `{id,question,resolution:"clarified"|"assumed",assumptionId}` covering every recorded question; `assumed` needs `assumptionId==id` and a recorded `request assume`; `clarified` needs a user clarification.
- GF-ARC-1 (`schemas/gf-architecture.schema.json`): `components[>=1]{id,responsibility>=5,group in api|backend|db|security|frontend|test|delivery}`, `dataFlow[>=1]{from,to (component id or external:<name>),via>=3,data>=3}`, `techChoices[>=1]{id,topic>=3,chosen,alternatives[>=2]{id,whyNot>=10},decision}`; refused: duplicate ids, one decision for two choices, chosen also listed as alternative, decision not a recorded `design.decision`, chosen differs from the decision's, an option not among the options the decision compared, decision without a rendered ADR.
Review evidence: `artifact:.eccode/artifacts/prd.json`. Approval takes the gate to `approved`; nothing is sealed yet.

### Gate 2 `design` (technical-designer; technical-reviewer AND security-reviewer): files `contracts/openapi.json db-schema.json migrations-plan.json access-matrix.json fixtures.json`, `spec.md`, `.eccode/artifacts/threat-model.json`
Start: `gate start design --actor orchestrator --reviewers technical-reviewer,security-reviewer`.
- GF-CON-1 OpenAPI 3.x JSON (`lib/greenfield/openapi.js`): `openapi` "3.x", `info.title`, `info.version`; non-empty `paths`; paths start with `/`; no path item `$ref`; unknown path-item keys refused (only methods, parameters, summary, description, servers, x-*); every operation: unique `operationId` matching `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`, `responses` with a 2xx and a 4xx|default, each response except 204/205/304 with `content.application/json.schema` that is NOT vacuous (not `{}` or annotation-only), `requestBody` (if present) with a non-vacuous JSON schema; security: global `security` + `components.securitySchemes` entry, or `x-gf-public: true` (public operations); `security:[{}]` refused unless public; all `$ref` local and resolving; `x-gf-internal: true` exempts an operation from PRD coverage.
- GF-CON-2 (`gf-db-schema`, `gf-migrations-plan` schemas): tables `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` each with a primaryKey column; column type in integer|text|boolean|datetime|float|json|uuid; `references` resolve; migration steps `{id,order,slice,description>=5,creates[],up>=5,down>=5,alters?}` with strictly increasing `order`; every table created by exactly ONE step.
- GF-CON-3 `access-matrix.json` `{roles:[{name ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$,level>=0}],cells:[{role,operationId,ownership:own|other|none,expected:allow|deny}]}`: a role `anonymous` at level 0; COMPLETE over role x operation x ownership (ownership own+other for operations with a path parameter, `none` otherwise), no duplicates, no extras; anonymous `allow` iff the operation is `x-gf-public`.
- GF-CON-4 `fixtures.json` `{roles:{<role>:{login:{operationId,body}|headers:{}}},ids?:{}}`: roles exist in the matrix; `anonymous` is `{}`; login operation exists; at least one non-anonymous role with login or headers. `events.json` optional (`{events:[{name,producer,consumers[>=1],schema}]}`).
- GF-CON-5: every http/flow criterion's `operationId` exists in the OpenAPI and its `as` role in the matrix; every non-internal operation is called by some criterion.
- GF-THR-1 `threat-model.json` (`gf-threat-model`): `assets[>=1]`, `trustBoundaries[>=1]{id,description,crosses[operationIds]}`, `threats[>=1]{id,boundary,category STRIDE word (spoofing|tampering|repudiation|information-disclosure|denial-of-service|elevation-of-privilege),description>=10,mitigation:{ref:contract|criterion|component,id}}`, `inputValidation[{operationId,field,rules>=3}]`, `accessMatrixSha256` (= sha256 of the exact bytes of `contracts/access-matrix.json`, 64 hex). Refused: an operation behind no boundary; a boundary crossing an unknown op; a mitigation pointing at nothing; inputValidation missing or extra against the GENERATED field list (`path:x`, `query:x`, `header:x`, `body:a.b` leaves to depth 3, for EVERY operation, including path params from the path template); stale matrix hash.
Review evidence: technical-reviewer `artifact:contracts/openapi.json`, security-reviewer `artifact:.eccode/artifacts/threat-model.json`.
CONTRACT FREEZE concretely: the five (six) `contracts/*.json` files are hashed (sha256 of bytes) in the approved design submission; at the plan approval the seal copies each to `.eccode/contracts/<sha>.json` and records the hashes. No OpenAPI conformance test, mock or generated contract test exists (E).

### Gate 3 `plan` (delivery-lead; technical-reviewer): files `plan.json` FIRST, `breakdown.json`, `estimates.json`
- `plan.json` (`schemas/plan.schema.json`): `{phases:[{id ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$,name>=3,goal>=10,acceptanceCriteria[>=1]}],tasks:[{id ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$,phase,title>=5,owner,dependencies[],inputs[],outputs[>=1],files[>=1],acceptanceCriteria[>=1],verification:{method>=5,command?}}]}`. Frozen checks: owner is a configured role, deps exist and not from a later phase, no cycle, every phase has a task. It MUST contain EXACTLY the tasks of the FIRST slice of breakdown.json (same owner, same file list; GF-WBS-1). So only the first slice becomes engine tasks: for S3 use ONE slice. [C+V]
- GF-WBS-1/2/3 `breakdown.json` (`gf-breakdown`): `groups[>=1]{name (a GROUPS key),roles[>=1] (must belong to that group),globs[>=1],denyGlobs[]}`, `slices[>=1]{id,goal>=10,criteria[],operations[],tasks[>=1]}`, `tasks[>=1]{id,title>=5,slice,group,owner (in the group's roles),files[>=1],dependencies[],estLines int>=1,provides?,consumes?,criteria?}`. Rules: every task file covered by its group's globs and not denied; `estLines <= plan.maxLinesPerTask (150)`; no dependency on a later slice, no cycle; slice/task lists agree. WBS-2: group globs pairwise disjoint (overlap only when inner is inside outer AND outer denies it); RESERVED: a group named `api` MUST own `contracts/**` and `mocks/**`, a group named `test` MUST own `tests/acceptance/**`, nobody else may overlap those ("group api must own contracts/**"). WBS-3: every PRD criterion in a slice's `criteria` AND in the `criteria` of >=1 task of group `test`; every OpenAPI operation `provides`-ed by EXACTLY ONE `backend`-group task and listed in exactly one slice whose index matches that task's slice. So even the "backend+test" S3 needs an `api` group in `groups` (it may have no tasks).
- GF-EST-1 `estimates.json` `{label:"agent-estimate-uncalibrated",basis>=40 chars,groups:{<group>:{tasks:int,minutes:{low,high},tokens:{low,high}}}}`: one entry per group that HAS tasks (exact task count), none for groups without tasks, low<=high.
- Plan-gate review approval re-validates all three gates at their approved hashes (GF-ART-DRIFT if a file changed since approval; GF-SEAL-1 "G1 cannot be sealed on this approval"), registers the estimate (`gf.estimate.registered`, immutable) and SEALS (`gf.g1.sealed`): sha256 of every approved stage artifact incl. `prd.json` and `breakdown.json`, snapshots of the contracts, `contractsHash` = sha256 over sorted `path:sha` lines of `contracts/*` + prd.json. If the seal fails after approval: restore the file, `eccode-gf seal --actor orchestrator`. After the seal never edit `breakdown.json` (bytes must equal the seal or every group write is refused, GF-OWN-1) and never edit `contracts/*` except via amendment. [V]

## C. After the seal

Task claim chain [V]: `gate start phase:<phaseId> --actor orchestrator` (needs seal + registered estimate: GF-SEAL-1 / GF-EST-1) -> `task claim <id> --actor <owner role>` (`GATE_BLOCKED` if the phase gate is pending; `OWNERSHIP` if actor != owner; `DEPENDENCY_PENDING`; `OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT` for overlapping globs of active claims; `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` at 4; `CHECKPOINT_DUE`; `AMBIGUITY_OPEN`; RETRY_LIMIT after 3 attempts).

Per task, the order that works [V]: claim -> write files (D) -> `run` (verification) -> `commit` -> `task complete`. `commit` is refused once the task is done.
1. `run --actor <role> --label <l> --task <id> --command "<cmd>" [--purpose check|reproduction]` (exit 0 only if passed and no problems). A command is accepted if (a) it equals, after trim, a task's `verification.command` from ANY plan task (then it runs via `sh -c` in the sandbox, so shell syntax is allowed), or (b) it is a pinned form: words separated by single spaces, only `[A-Za-z0-9_./:=,@+-]`, paths relative inside the project (never `.eccode`):
   - pytest: `pytest|python -m pytest|python3 -m pytest` + `-q -x -v -rA --tb=short|line|no --maxfail=<n> -k <word> --cov=<path> --cov-report=term` + paths/node ids. Use `python -m pytest tests/unit -q` (bare `pytest` does not put the project root on sys.path: ModuleNotFoundError app). `-p ...` is refused. [V]
   - app start: `serve <module>:<attr> --port <1024-65535> -- <pytest form|playwright form>`, e.g. `serve app.main:app --port 18765 -- python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_x.py`. Starts `python -m uvicorn` on 127.0.0.1, waits 20 s, runs the check, kills the server. [V as --actor orchestrator]. As a GROUP role under Landlock it FAILS: bind EACCES, exit 125 "did not answer" (TCP denied). Run `serve` as `--actor orchestrator` (copy runner; DB files it creates stay in the copy and are discarded). [V]
   - alembic: `upgrade|downgrade <rev>`, `current|history|heads|check`, `revision --autogenerate -m <word>` (writes migrations/, owner of migrations/ only). ruff: `ruff check [--output-format=concise|full|json] <paths>`, `ruff check --fix <paths>`, `ruff format [--check] <paths>`. semgrep/gitleaks/trivy forms exist but the tools are not installed. playwright forms exist.
   - Not accepted (GF-RUN-2): `;`, `&&`, `|`, `$`, quotes, any other flag (`ruff check --no-cache` is NOT pinned-form; pin it in plan.json instead), `python -c`. Result JSON: `{evidence:"ev:<id>",status,exitCode,outputTail,problems[],copiedBack[],discarded[],syncedIn[],isolation{}}`. [V]
   - Sandbox facts [V]: cwd is `.gf-worktrees/<group>` (a HEAD checkout plus the group's own files synced in); only the group's owned directories + a private $TMPDIR are writable, so a `.ruff_cache` write fails (`Failed to initialize cache ... Permission denied`) unless the plan-pinned command uses `--no-cache`, pytest only warns about its cache; no network; env scrubbed to PATH, LANG, TERM, TZ, VIRTUAL_ENV, ECCODE_GF_PYTHON (add names via `config.gf.sandboxEnv:[...]`); default SQLite path `./app.db` is unwritable for non-owners, put the default DB in `tempfile.gettempdir()` or use `sqlite://`.
2. `commit --actor <role> --task <id> [--message t]`: commits exactly the group's changed files (validated against the ownership map and the claimed task's `files`, regular files, no symlinks, one hard link) onto `refs/heads/gf/<group>` by git plumbing; refused (GF-ISO-2) for a file outside the task's files, another group's file (GF-OWN-2), or "nothing to commit". Run it again after every later edit. [V]
3. `task complete <id> --actor <owner> --file <handoff.json>`. Handoff schema (`schemas/handoff.schema.json`, no extra keys) [V]:
```
{ "from":"<actor>", "to":"delivery-lead", "task":"<id>", "objective":">=10", "context":">=10", "inputs":[...], "expectedOutput":">=5",
  "acceptanceCriteria":[">=1 of >=3"], "completedWork":">=10", "filesChanged":["rel/path",...], "evidence":["ev:<id>",...], "remainingIssues":[], "nextAction":">=5",
  "testsNotNeeded"?: ">=10", "newDependencies"?: [{name,reason>=10,alternativesChecked[>=1 of >=5],manifest?}], "shortcuts"?: [{file,limit,upgradeWhen}] }
```
   Refused when [V/C]: `handoff.task/from` mismatch; `evidence` lacks a PASSING command run recorded after the claim; if the task has `verification.command`, the cited passing run must be that exact command (whitespace-normalised, "staged verification"); a filesChanged entry outside the task's `files` or the group's paths (GF-OWN-3: "belongs to <group>"); a listed file git shows unchanged since claim; lean (level full): code files changed without a test file in the same task and no `testsNotNeeded` ("lean: code changed ... but no test file did"), undeclared new dependency, undeclared shortcut marker; bug-pattern scan; breaking change (removed export/route, edited migration) without `breakingChanges`; budget: more than 3 files (`plan.maxFilesPerTask`) or 150 changed lines per task ("over the budget of 3", fix: split the task, or `eccode task waive-budget <task> --reason "<>=15>" --actor orchestrator`). `filesChanged` must list only non-`.eccode` files that really changed.
4. Every 3 completed tasks (while more remain) `CHECKPOINT_DUE`: `eccode evidence run --actor orchestrator --label cp --json -- <cmd>` then `eccode plan checkpoint --evidence ev:<id> --actor orchestrator`. [V]
5. `merge --actor orchestrator --scope <s> --checks ev:<id>,ev:<id>` (orchestrator or user): each id must be a recorded PASSED evidence; merges every `gf/<group>` into the CURRENT branch in dependency order of the groups (from task deps), in memory; refuses a conflict (GF-ISO-3, "GF-OWN violation signal"), a detached HEAD, "no group branch has anything to merge". HEAD moves; working tree is untouched. Run it as soon as a group's code must be visible to another group: a group's `run` sees only HEAD plus its own files, so tests of group `test` cannot import `app` until `merge` (verified ModuleNotFoundError before, fine after with `python -m pytest`). [V]
6. `deps install --actor orchestrator --command "<form>"`: forms ONLY `pip install -r <file>`, `python -m pip install -r <file>`, `python3 -m pip install -r <file>`, `npm ci`, `uv sync`, `poetry install` (no extra flags; put `--only-binary=:all:` and hashes inside the requirements file). Network allowed, writable only `node_modules .venv venv vendor` (it mkdirs them). Records lockfile hashes. With the prebuilt venv first on PATH it passes ("already satisfied"); installs elsewhere fail read-only. The venv exists, so S3 normally needs no install. [V]
7. Phase gate (optional for closure, normal for the frozen record) [V]: `gate submit phase:<id> --actor delivery-lead` (auto-includes the tasks' changed files; all tasks must be done), then reviewer records its OWN passing check `eccode evidence run --actor technical-reviewer --label rc -- <cmd>` and `gate review phase:<id> --actor technical-reviewer --file r.json` citing that `ev:` id. A rejection must cite an `ev:` of a failing run or `file:line` in `detail`.
8. Other: `message send --actor <role> --to <group,..> --kind question|answer|amendment-request|blocker|decision|handoff --subject <3-200> --body <=4096 B> [--in-reply-to <id>]`; `message list [--from g --to g --kind k]`. Contract change [V]: `message send --kind amendment-request --to api` -> `amend request --actor <role> --contract contracts/openapi.json --reason t --message <msg id> --proposed t` -> the api group edits the file (hook allows it only while a request is open AND the api role has a claimed task: with no api task in the plan the orchestrator must edit it) -> `amend apply --actor technical-reviewer --request <id> --reason "<>=30>"` (file must be valid and changed; classified additive|breaking). `ownership show`; `ownership amend --actor <reviewer> --group g --to glob,glob --reason "<>=30>" --message <msg id>`. `task rescope <t> --files .. --reason ..` is the USER's for a reviewed plan (headless `ECCODE_HEADLESS=1`: orchestrator, recorded as assumption). `estimate revise --actor orchestrator|delivery-lead --reason t --file groups.json` (`{<group>:{tasks,minutes:{low,high},tokens:{low,high}}}`). `attribute --base <commit>` (exit 2 if a changed path is unowned or undeclared: use the sealed-G1 housekeeping commit as base, otherwise `.gitignore`/`contracts/**` are listed). `audit [--json]` exit 2 on errors; warnings L-GF-17 are normal without install. [V]

### Slice closure (`close *`, scope = any string, e.g. `S3`) [V end to end]
Needs a clean tree (see friction 1). Order: battery 1 -> 3 dispatches+reviews -> battery 2 -> `close slice`.
- `close battery --actor orchestrator --scope S3 --test "python -m pytest tests/unit -q -x" --base <commit> --max 20`: frozen mutation tool; mutates lines ADDED since `base` (python operators), runs the test command in the real tree via sh (must pass on unmodified code), tree clean before and after, total>0. Records a numbered round (1,2,...). Each survivor key (`file:line:op`) needs an accepted reason at close.
- `close dispatch --actor orchestrator --scope S3 --role <reviewer role> --step comprehension|critique|readiness --input <relpath>,<relpath>` -> prints `disp-...` id (use `--json`). Inputs: regular project files, not under `.eccode/{drafts,handoffs,memory,runs,lab,improvements}` nor events.jsonl/state.json. One dispatch = one review. Bound to the tree hash.
- `close review --actor <that role> --scope S3 --step <step> --dispatch <id> --summary-file <f> [--findings <f.json>] [--verdict go|no-go] [--evidence ev:<id>,path:line]`. Summary >=100 chars. comprehension/critique: verdict derived (`clean` without findings), findings file = JSON list `{id (unique in the whole record),severity:"blocking|major|minor",kind:"documentation" (comprehension) | "defect" (critique),summary>=10}`. readiness: `--verdict go|no-go` and >=1 citation (`ev:<id>` passed, or `path:line` existing at that tree). Reviewer role must have authored nothing (no claim/complete/gate submit) and may not be the closer; a no-go stands until the tree changes.
- `close resolve --actor <a> --finding <id> --resolution fixed|withdrawn|deferred [--proof-run ev:<id> --reproduction ev:<id>] [--reason t>=30] [--limit L-GF-n]`. fixed (defect) = post-fix evidence of `eccode fix verify --actor <a> --base <ref> --test "<cmd>"` whose pre-fix run failed as a reproduction at a commit with the finding's tree; fixed (documentation) = `--reproduction` (failed run recorded with `--purpose reproduction`) + `--proof-run` (same command passed). withdrawn = the raising reviewer only. deferred = `--actor user`, minor (or major documentation) only. A fix changes the tree, so a new round of all three steps on the fixed tree follows (and a new last battery).
- `close status --scope S3` lists what blocks closure. `close slice --actor orchestrator|user --scope S3 --accounting acc.json [--accepted acc2.json]`:
  `acc.json` = `{"unit":"all-processed-tokens","start":<int>|"unmeasurable","end":<int>|"unmeasurable"}` (end>=start); `acc2.json` = `[{"key":"<survivor key of the LAST battery>","reason":"<>=30 chars>"}]`.
  Requires: valid comprehension, critique, readiness(go) on the closing tree; every finding resolved; >=2 batteries, first before the first review, last on the closing tree after the last fix.
- Owner acceptance instead (`--actor user` only): `close accept --scope S3 --accepted f.json`, `f.json` = `[{"finding":"<id>","severity":"<recorded>","limit":"L-GF-<n>","reason":"<>=30>"}]` listing EVERY open finding, no blocking one, non-empty.

## D. Where files live; worktrees and branches [V]
- Group source files live in the REAL project tree at their owned paths (`app/**`, `tests/**`, `migrations/**`, ...). A group role writes them with the harness Write/Edit tools (or the orchestrator writes them as that role in unmanaged mode). `.gf-worktrees/<group>/` is only a scratch checkout the engine builds for `run`: `git worktree add --detach <root>/.gf-worktrees/<group> HEAD` on first run, then `checkout --detach HEAD; reset --hard; clean -fdx` before each run, the group's owned files copied in from the real tree, and after the run the group's changed owned files copied back. Dependency dirs are symlinked in. Never author in a worktree.
- Branch `refs/heads/gf/<group>` is created by the first `commit` from HEAD (later commits stack on its tip); the integration branch is whatever branch the real tree is on; `merge` writes a merge commit per group there.
- The engine writes `/.gf-worktrees/` into `.git/info/exclude` only. The closure's clean-tree check ignores info/exclude, so commit a `.gitignore` that lists `.gf-worktrees/` (and `__pycache__/ .pytest_cache/ .ruff_cache/ *.pyc *.db`). Files owned by no group (`.gitignore`, `requirements.txt`, `pytest.ini`) and `contracts/*` (authored by the design author, not a group) are committed by the orchestrator with plain git; `attribute` will list them unless the base is after that commit.
- Hook behavior when wired [V by feeding PreToolUse JSON to `scripts/hooks/guard.js`]: a group subagent may Write/Edit only inside a CLAIMED task's `files` AND its group's globs (GF-OWN-2; else "has no claimed task" / "belongs to <group>"), drafts only under `.eccode/drafts/<group>/`, no shell at all (GF-RUN-1); document authors write only `.eccode/artifacts/**` and `.eccode/drafts/**`, so technical-designer CANNOT write `contracts/*.json` directly (the orchestrator, role-less main session, copies them in); reviewers write `.eccode/reviews/drafts/**`. The hook matcher has no Read: reading is never blocked.

## E. Generators and acceptance hooks: what exists
- NO contract-test generator, NO mock server, NO OpenAPI-to-pytest generator, NO conformance check of the running app against the sealed OpenAPI. Existing helpers only: `lib/greenfield/openapi.js` (validator, operation index, request-field list, differ/classifier), `lib/greenfield/jsonschema.js` (subset validator), frozen `eccode guard api|migration` and `scripts/guards/{openapi_dump,schema_dump}.py` (frozen guards, not wired to the sealed contracts, not on the group allowlist). [C]
- NO GF-ACC-1/2 code (no acceptance baseline/amend events, no sealing of a hidden suite, no red-run check): grep finds GF-ACC only in docs. The hidden suite must be held outside the repo by the orchestrator; the hook has no Read matcher, so location is the only protection. To run it: a clean clone/worktree of the delivered commit plus your own shell, or `eccode-gf run --actor orchestrator --command "serve app.main:app --port <n> -- python -m pytest -q <relpath>"` (needs a project-relative path; absolute/outside paths are refused) [I for the hidden-suite use; the serve form itself [V]].
- `test` group owns `tests/**` in the probe breakdown (reserved `tests/acceptance/**` is the test group's by rule), so the builders' own tests live in `tests/unit/**`; keep them separate from the hidden suite for B3.

## F. Minimal run, exact order (all [V] in p2 unless marked)
```
ENV: export PATH=/root/.cache/eccode/phase3-venv/bin:$PATH ECCODE_GF_PYTHON=/root/.cache/eccode/phase3-venv/bin/python
GF="node /home/user/ECCode/bin/eccode-gf.js --root $P"; ECC="node /home/user/ECCode/bin/eccode.js --root $P"
 1 git init $P; git commit --allow-empty -m init
 2 $GF isolation check                                   (must print: group mode available)
 3 $GF init --name N --idea "<text>"
 4 write PRD/architecture artifacts; $ECC design alternatives|decide|adr per tech choice (2 choices in the probe); edit decision ids into architecture.json
 5 $GF validate architecture --artifact brief.md --artifact prd.json --artifact architecture.json
 6 $GF gate start architecture --actor orchestrator; gate submit architecture --actor product-architect --artifact ...; gate review architecture --actor architecture-reviewer --file r.json
 7 write contracts/*.json + spec.md + threat-model.json; validate design; gate start design --actor orchestrator --reviewers technical-reviewer,security-reviewer; gate submit design --actor technical-designer ...; gate review design (technical-reviewer, then security-reviewer)
 8 write plan.json, breakdown.json (ONE slice, groups api+backend+test), estimates.json; validate plan; gate start plan; gate submit plan --actor delivery-lead --artifact plan.json --artifact breakdown.json --artifact estimates.json; gate review plan --actor technical-reviewer   -> seal
 9 .gitignore (.gf-worktrees/ ...) + contracts committed by the orchestrator (git add; git commit)       ; $GF status (sealed:true); $GF audit
10 hidden suite written by a separate agent OUTSIDE the repo (no engine step) [I]
11 $GF gate start phase:<phaseId> --actor orchestrator
12 per task: task claim -> write files -> run (plan-pinned verification command, exact string) -> commit -> task complete (handoff with testsNotNeeded for backend code) ; after 3 done: evidence run + plan checkpoint
13 merge --actor orchestrator --scope S3 --checks ev:<passed id>  (as soon as another group needs the code; and at the end)
14 gate submit phase:<id>; reviewer evidence run; gate review phase:<id> (optional)
15 orchestrator: serve ... -- python -m pytest ... (HTTP-level check) ; hidden suite in a clean checkout [I]
16 commit housekeeping; tree clean; close battery #1; close dispatch x3; close review x3; close battery #2; close slice --accounting acc.json --accepted acc2.json
17 $GF audit (must be OK); $GF attribute --base <sealed-G1 commit>
```
Top friction points (a correct action refused), rule/code and fix:
1. Closure "the tree is not clean (.gf-worktrees/backend/, ...)" (GF-CLOSE-1/3/5 and GF-CLOSE-6): commit a `.gitignore` containing `.gf-worktrees/` before any dispatch/battery. [V]
2. `GF-ISO-2: task X is not claimed by <role> (status done)`: `commit` must precede `task complete`. Recovery: `$ECC task reset X --actor orchestrator --reason "..."`, re-claim, rerun, commit, complete. [V]
3. `INVALID_HANDOFF ... lean: code changed (...) but no test file did`: backend tasks cannot ship tests (other group): add `"testsNotNeeded":"<>=10 chars>"`; also the handoff must cite a passing `ev:` recorded after the claim, and for a pinned `verification.command` that exact command. [V]
4. `CHECKPOINT_DUE` at the 4th claim (every 3 done): `evidence run --actor orchestrator ... -- <cmd>` then `plan checkpoint --evidence ev:<id>`. [V]
5. Task budget (`over the budget of 3` files / 150 lines): plan tasks of <=3 files and estLines <150, or `task waive-budget`. A breakdown cannot use `app/**` as one task. [C]
6. `serve` as a group role: bind EACCES / `GF-ISO-0 ... unverifiable here` (Landlock denies TCP; no bwrap): run `serve` as `--actor orchestrator`. [V]
7. `GF-RUN-2: flag -p is not in the pinned form` / `... contains shell syntax`: use only the listed forms or pin the exact command in plan.json `verification.command`; `pytest` alone fails `No module named app`: use `python -m pytest`. [V]
8. ruff in the sandbox: cache dir Permission denied (pin `ruff check --no-cache <files>` in the plan) and ruff 0.16.9 default rules flag FastAPI `Depends()` defaults (B008), `Optional[...]` (UP045), stale `# noqa` (RUF100): write `Annotated[...]` aliases, `X | None`, no unused noqa, or pin `--select E,F`. The plan is sealed, so decide the pinned commands BEFORE the plan gate. [V]
9. A group's `run` cannot see other groups' uncommitted code: `merge` first (cites `--checks ev:<passed id>`); a second merge with nothing new is `GF-ISO-3: no group branch has anything to merge`; after editing a file re-`commit` before `merge`, otherwise the tracked tree differs and closure is refused. [V]
10. G1: `GF-WBS-2 group api must own contracts/**` (and test must own tests/acceptance/**) even for a "backend+test" project; `GF-WBS-3` criterion without a test-group task / operation with !=1 backend provider; `GF-THR-1` on design start without both reviewers; `GF-CON-3` incomplete matrix; plan.json must be first, only the first slice; `MISSING_SECTIONS` when no `.md` with the required headings is submitted. Also `GF-SEAL-1` on claim before the seal, `GATE_BLOCKED ... phase gate is pending` before `gate start phase:<id>`. [V/C]
Also: `GF-CLOSE-3 survivor <key> has no accepted reason` (supply `--accepted`), `close status` always lists survivors (it takes no `--accepted`), reviewer who ever claimed/completed/submitted cannot review a close step, `GF-OWN-1` after editing the sealed `breakdown.json`.

## G. Required by the S3 protocol / handoff but NOT implemented (design only)
- Contract-test generator (pytest from the sealed OpenAPI), mock server, GF-FE-1, GF-FRZ-3/4 (conformance of `app.openapi()` and the migrated DB to the sealed files), GF-API-1..4 (error shape, `/v1`, DTO allowlist, runtime output validation): none exist (section 20 "S3, reduced"). The seal protects the contract FILES only.
- GF-ACC-1/2 and the "hidden suite sealed by hash, write/read-denied to groups, run once by the engine in a clean checkout": no code. No Read denial (hook matcher lacks Read, L-GF-7). No engine command runs a suite held outside the repo.
- Slices as work items (`gf slice open|integrate`), `gf.slice.*` events, `verify-done` / DONE gate, GF-OWN-4 inside the audit, GF-CONF-1 slice-open writing `behavior.json/guards.json/security.json` (only `config pin` exists), G0.5 reference search/ADR (S3 protocol records "scratch" as an ADR: the operator must record it as a normal `design` decision or in `brief.md`; the engine does not check it), the cost governor GF-COST, UX spec, G1.5 problem register.
- Only the FIRST breakdown slice becomes engine tasks; later slices need a new work item that is not built, so S3 must be one slice.
- Usage metering: `lib/greenfield/usage.js` is a library (`require`), not a CLI, and reads the harness transcript; no `eccode-gf` command takes the snapshots the handoff asks for [C].
- Metric 4 (friction vs capability refusals): refusals are not logged by the engine; the operator logs them.
- Real per-group subagents need `eccode install` (managed-path), where group roles have no shell and use the MCP tools `gf_run`, `gf_commit`, `task_claim`, `task_complete`, `gf_message_send` of their own role-locked server [C]; the S3 handoff's `--actor` CLI commands are what the orchestrator runs, and under profile `no-shell` Bash is denied to it as well [V in settings.json]. Not run end to end here.
